verdict.rationale: The docs show interrupts pausing graph execution at specific points to wait for external input. Execution resumes by re-invoking the graph with Command, whose value becomes the return value of interrupt(). Checkpointers persist the exact state so the run can pick up later, and breakpoints are configured at compile time. A community user independently confirms LangGraph's human-in-the-loop state machine lets an analyst correct a step and continue. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of approve/reject/edit patterns for approving tool calls, and hands-on verification of the pause/resume flow.
